title: Why spamming lateral raises won't work
summary: NH argues that the influencer advice to spam lateral raises several times a week for big shoulders is counterproductive: growth comes from progression, not frequency, and isolation lifts progress slowly while excess frequency eats recovery. He recommends pairing presses with lateral raises (about 2:1 isolation to compound), training the muscle when recovered, and adding volume or variations only when progress stalls, noting that success stories are newbie gains or PED users.
claims: Spamming lateral raises for shoulders is trendy because it is simple, but it often sabotages growth
A spammable lift is one you can train 2-4 times a week; compounds taken close to failure cannot hit that frequency, so only isolation lifts qualify
Doing a movement does not make a muscle grow; progressing on it does, so more frequency only helps if it produces progression
Isolation lifts recruit little muscle so they progress slowly and plateau quickly; you will never add 50 lb to one in a year
Raising frequency to force progress on a stalled isolation lift cuts recovery and keeps the lagging muscle fatigued, so it stays lagging
Lagging muscles lack work capacity and tire quickly; that work capacity must be built first, which requires recovery between sessions
The muscle dictates how often it can be trained; hitting a muscle more than 2-3 times a week is something you earn
Obsessing over a weak point with excessive frequency creates frustration that kills enjoyment and keeps it weak
Train the target muscle whenever it is recovered and able to perform, putting progression and recovery first
Compounds progress much faster: you can add weight every session or every other session, while a curl may stay at the same weight for 3-4 weeks
Spamming lateral raises usually forces you to drop horizontal presses, removing the lift that would give the biggest shoulder gains and support lateral raise progress
Use about a 2:1 ratio of isolation to compound work for a muscle; that beats isolation only, and compound only also misses out
Muscle built by pressing carries over to lateral raises, so the two lifts feed each other in a virtuous circle; a single movement hits diminishing returns
Progress on a press and a lateral raise as long as possible; when progress stops, add volume or frequency through variations or rotations
Shoulder transformations from spamming lateral raises are newbie gains; when untrained, any method works
Frequency is capped by the days in the week, so a method based on adding frequency cannot sustain progress into intermediate and advanced stages
The guys in these transformation videos are usually not big; they are only a few steps ahead of the teenagers watching
PEDs enhance recovery so enhanced lifters can spam isolation work and grow; naturals should ignore their frequency advice
